model_reported.summary: Proposed per-timestep OpenMP teams to contrast with the previously measured persistent-team candidate while preserving row ownership and timestep completion.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: The proposed contrast uses the already measured OpenMP approach; no additional hardware or software fact is needed to select it.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: The candidate uses basic OpenMP worksharing and its implicit completion barrier; the prior OpenMP candidate was controller-validated, and no uncertain API property requires a new reference.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared the supplied valid means cautiously, noted the catalog's single distinct program, and left the per-step versus persistent and one-/four-thread comparison to controller measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use this as a baseline for comparing per-step and persistent OpenMP team lifetimes on the same target and thread budgets.
memory_lessons.claim: The persistent-team candidate was valid and measured faster than the serial baseline in the supplied trials, but those measurements do not establish whether the repeated fork/join overhead differs from per-step teams.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this per-step-team candidate and compare it with the persistent-team candidate at one and four threads under the same protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: The prior persistent-team candidate was valid and measured at 0.241645 seconds versus the valid serial baseline at 0.464905 seconds, but it did not isolate team lifetime. This contrasting implementation creates a team for each timestep, with static work over disjoint z/y rows and an implicit completion barrier before the next step. If repeated team creation is costly, it should be slower than the persistent-team version; at one thread the overhead may dominate. Controller measurements at one and four threads, including initialization, are needed to test this.

retained: Create an OpenMP parallel-for team inside each stencil timestep, requesting no more than the supplied positive thread budget.
Distribute disjoint z/y rows with static collapse(2), preserving contiguous x traversal.
Rely on each parallel-for's completion before the following timestep reads its input buffer; retain the existing timestep parity, initialization, bounds, and boundary behavior.
